**Why it degrades this way**
- Lower permeability cuts the productivity index (field `productivity_index_m3h_per_bar`): 12.22 at 200 mD versus 3.055 at 50 mD. At the same 287.5 m3/h per doublet that means drawdown rises from 23.53 bar to 94.1 bar and ESP power from 471.5 kW to 1277 kW (reservoir_simulation, analytic). Injector wellhead pressure rises from 26.07 bar to 96.65 bar.
- The 40 K brine-cooling limit is already binding at every permeability (max_brine_cooling_k = 40.0 in all runs), so the plant cannot compensate by extracting more heat per cubic metre — it pumps less brine and burns more gas. At 30 mD the boiler supplies 13360 MWh/yr and co-produced gas 11780 MWh/yr (R0071); at 10 mD geothermal covers only 50.37 % of heat (R0074).
- Flow stays inside the 50-300 m3/h rule even at 10 mD (87.5 m3/h), so the failure mode is cost, not infeasibility.

**Robustness verdict**
- **Safe zone: 100 mD and above** — LCOE 42.12 or less, CO2 6553 t/yr or less, still clearly better than gas-only.
- **Marginal: 30-50 mD** — LCOE 47.27 to 54.02, still below the 62.77 gas-only proxy but the margin is thin.
- **Break-even around 20 mD** (LCOE 61.07 vs 62.77). Below that the geothermal plant is more expensive than the gas-only proxy, though it still emits less CO2 (12950 vs 27240 t/yr at 20 mD).
- Adding a third doublet does not rescue low permeability: at 30 mD, 3D-3100m-boiler-electric gives LCOE 61.19 (R0075) versus 54.02 for two doublets — worse, because you pay capex for wells that each run at low flow.

The dry cooler model is in and registered.

**What it is** — `dry_cooler` / class `DryCooler` in module `dry_cooler_model`. Interface: water inlet temperature, water flow (m³/s), air temperature in; heat rejected (W), water outlet temperature, fan power, effectiveness out.

**Physics** — effectiveness on the water capacity rate: ε = ε_max·(1 − exp(−k/flow)) with k = UA/(ρc_p) = 0.03 m³/s, ε_max 0.95, fan power 2 % of rejected heat. Output temperature is computed from the energy balance, so heat_rejected = ρc_p·flow·ΔT exactly; it returns zero when flow is zero or air is not colder than the water, and the outlet stays between air and inlet temperature.

What is happening: at lower permeability the wells deliver less for the same drawdown, so the plant pumps harder — maximum ESP differential pressure rises to 114.2 bar at 50 mD (R0085) and 157.8 bar at 20 mD (R0087) — and below about 30 mD the geothermal side can no longer carry the full heat load, so the gas boiler picks up the rest. I screened 48 designs (1–3 doublets × depths 2500/3100 m × boiler/heat-pump upgrade × absorption/electric chillers × with/without CHP) [R0049].

**Recommended design [R0028]: 2 doublets at 3100 m, boiler top-up, electric chiller + CHP**
- LCOE €36.88/MWh vs €36.10/MWh for the cheapest 1-doublet design [R0012] — a difference of €0.78/MWh, i.e. 2.16% higher [compare: R0028 vs R0012]
- All hard rules pass: heating (111.7 GWh/yr) and cooling (23.74 GWh/yr) demand met every day, 50–300 m³/h per doublet, ≤40 K brine cooling, ≤330 doublet-days, production = injection
- Meets **93% of heat geothermally** (103.8 GWh/yr) with only 685 MWh/yr boiler gas and 29 MWh/yr purchased gas [R0028]
- **CO₂: 5,358 t/yr vs 10,280 t/yr for the 1-doublet design — 47.9% lower** (−4,922 t/yr) [compare: R0028 vs R0012]

All absorption-chiller-only designs failed the "cooling demand met" check (e.g. 1D-2500m-boiler-absorption), so the chiller must be electric. Reservoir at 3100 m: 105°C, 310.6 bar, PI 12.22 m³/h/bar [R0028].

Why 2 doublets: each doublet may run at most 330 days/yr, and with a 30 MW heating peak one doublet alone can't cover the full year, so the 1-doublet design burns 28,340 MWh/yr of purchased gas [R0012]. Two staggered doublets keep one producing every day, cut purchased gas to 29 MWh/yr, and burn the co-produced gas (16,010 MWh/yr) in a CHP engine supplying 8,660 MWh/yr heat and 4,330 MWh/yr electricity [R0028].
